items.title: 63475_Arnett Cobb oral history interview
items.q: You know who gave me my credit reference in New York? Mr. Earl Bostic... I said, 'I'm a friend of Earl Bostick's.' And you know what the man said to me? He said, 'Any friend of Earl Bostick's is a friend of mine.'

ctx.x: And we're going downtown, and the Strand Theatre, and I bring some of the guys up, my close friends in the band that I'd been associated with, and they didn't have a chair to sit on. I'd say, 'Well, if they're my friends, they can sit on the floor, like me.' And they did ... and we had a ball. That's how you know who your friends are -- they accept you as you are. See, I didn't intend to pretend, because I was a Texas boy, and that's the way we lived in Texas. Honestly. So I said I'd invite them and if they were…

And when they left, me and my wife opened the couch out, and get in the bed together. I didn't have no credit references. Lionel and Gladys wouldn't give me any, and I'm working for him. You know who gave me my credit reference in New York? Mr. Earl Bostic. When I told him that they wouldn't recommend me for credit, he said, 'Meet me at Spears' on Third

Avenue at 10 o'clock." No, he didn't say 10 o'clock; he said we'll see what the half an hour is from Monday, and gone out, you know, for a half an hour. He said, "Now meet you at 10 o'clock." I said, "Okay. Thank you." I was at 10 o'clock, maybe it was a little behind, and I walked in the door, and I said, "I'm a friend of Earl Bostick's." And you know what the man said to me? He said, "Any friend of Earl Bostick's is a friend of mine. Come on in."
